text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Netanyahu, Arafat on verge of summit.
- U.S. slams settlement expansion.
- Soldiers anxious over drawn-out Hebron negotiations.
- Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani: We are responsible for border police violence.
- Israeli army sets up anti-guerrilla combat training school.
- Miracle declared in Bethlehem as Jesus "weeps".
- Comptroller: Government loan records inconsistent.
- Exports up 20 percent in October.
- Clal Israel profits plummet; Israel Corp slips into red.
- Koor, Electric Corp net down; Hapoalim Investments income up 13 percent.
GLOBES
- Improvement in exports and production; slowdown in import of needs.
- Heads of three concerns: Slowdown a result of monetary policy.
- 92 of the 1,400 companies operating abroad hold 85 percent of all real investments.
HAARETZ

- Netanyahu drafting new security policy, accuses late prime minister Rabin and successor Peres of blunders. Syrian ambassador in Cairo: If Israel will threaten us with nuclear weapons, we'll respond with chemical weapons.
- Palestinians reject Israeli compromise proposal on Israeli army freedom of action in Hebron.
- Budget department plan for an additional cut excludes proposals to raise taxes.
MAARIV
- Sharp improvement in economic activity -- industrial exports up 16.5 percent in two months.
- For the first time Syria threatens Israel with chemical weapons.
- Political sources in Jerusalem say it's hoped Hebron agreement can be initialed this week.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Draft report to prime minister on 1956 Suez crisis: There was a reciprocal murder of captives.
- For Hanukah, flights abroad are full.
- Poll of Labour party central committee members: 65 percent say Peres must retire in summer; 60 percent say Barak the suitable heir.
- At peak of tensions a number of weeks ago Peres passed a message to Syria's Assad: "Let's meet". Peres: It wasn't exactly a message.
- Israeli army buys equipment valued at billions of shekels in face of Syrian threat.
